\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{развод} (razvód)}{развод (razvód)}]{\ru{развод} (razvód) — a divorce}

\label{lesson:RU-C307-razvod}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a church wedding, then the Russian for to part.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{развод}}
\textbf{\ru{развод}} (\emph{razvód}) — \textquotedblleft{}a divorce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{После} \ru{развода} \ru{он} \ru{уехал} \ru{в} \ru{другой} \ru{город}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pósle razvóda on uyékhal v drugóy górod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the divorce he moved to another town.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{развод}} is built on \emph{\ru{разводить}} \textquotedblleft{}to lead apart\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{\ru{раз}-} and \emph{\ru{водить}} \textquotedblleft{}to lead\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Proto-Slavic \emph{voditi} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for a church wedding, then the Russian for to part, then say \emph{razvód} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{разводиться} (razvodítsya)}{разводиться (razvodítsya)}]{\ru{разводиться} (razvodítsya) — to get divorced}

\label{lesson:RU-C307-razvoditsya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to part, then the Russian for a divorce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{разводиться}}
\textbf{\ru{разводиться}} (\emph{razvodítsya}) — \textquotedblleft{}to get divorced\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Его} \ru{родители} \ru{развелись} \ru{давно}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Yevó rodíteli razvelís davnó.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His parents divorced long ago.
\end{quote}

Imperfective; the perfective is \emph{\ru{развестись}} (\emph{razvestís}), past \emph{\ru{развёлся}} (\emph{razvyólsya}), \emph{\ru{развелась}}. It takes \emph{\ru{с}} + instrumental.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{разводиться}} is built on \emph{\ru{раз}-} \textquotedblleft{}apart\textquotedblright{} and \emph{\ru{водить}} \textquotedblleft{}to lead\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Proto-Slavic \emph{voditi} (EtymDB), with the reflexive \emph{-\ru{ся}}: to be led apart.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{razvodítsya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{razvodítsya}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for to part, then the Russian for a divorce, then say \emph{razvodítsya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{переезд} (pereyézd)}{переезд (pereyézd)}]{\ru{переезд} (pereyézd) — a move (to a new home)}

\label{lesson:RU-C307-pereyezd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a divorce, then the Russian for to get divorced.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{переезд}}
\textbf{\ru{переезд}} (\emph{pereyézd}) — \textquotedblleft{}a move (to a new home)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Переезд} \ru{занял} \ru{целую} \ru{неделю}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pereyézd zányal tséluyu nedélyu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The move took a whole week.
\end{quote}

Also a level crossing. The verb is \emph{\ru{переезжать}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{переезд}} is built on \emph{\ru{переехать}} \textquotedblleft{}to move\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{\ru{пере}-} \textquotedblleft{}across\textquotedblright{} and \emph{\ru{ехать}} \textquotedblleft{}to go by vehicle\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Proto-Slavic \emph{ěxati} \textquotedblleft{}to travel\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{увольняться} (uvolnyátsya)}{увольняться (uvolnyátsya)}]{\ru{увольняться} (uvolnyátsya) — to quit (a job), to resign}

\label{lesson:RU-C307-uvolnyatsya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to get divorced, then the Russian for a move.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{увольняться}}
\textbf{\ru{увольняться}} (\emph{uvolnyátsya}) — \textquotedblleft{}to quit (a job), to resign\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Она} \ru{уволилась} \ru{и} \ru{открыла} \ru{своё} \ru{кафе}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Oná uvólilas i otkrýla svoyó kafé.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She quit her job and opened her own café.
\end{quote}

Imperfective; perfective \emph{\ru{уволиться}} (\emph{uvólitsya}). It takes \emph{\ru{с}} + genitive: \emph{\ru{уволиться} \ru{с} \ru{работы}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{увольняться}} is built on \emph{\ru{у}-} and \emph{\ru{воля}} \textquotedblleft{}will, freedom\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Proto-Slavic \emph{voľa}, from PIE \emph{welh\textsubscript{1}-} \textquotedblleft{}to choose, to wish\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): to set oneself free.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{наследство} (naslédstvo)}{наследство (naslédstvo)}]{\ru{наследство} (naslédstvo) — an inheritance}

\label{lesson:RU-C307-nasledstvo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a move, then the Russian for to quit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{наследство}}
\textbf{\ru{наследство}} (\emph{naslédstvo}) — \textquotedblleft{}an inheritance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Он} \ru{получил} \ru{в} \ru{наследство} \ru{старый} \ru{дом}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{On poluchíl v naslédstvo stáryy dom.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He inherited an old house.
\end{quote}

Neuter. \emph{\ru{Получить} \ru{в} \ru{наследство}} — to inherit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{\ru{наследство}} is built on \emph{\ru{наследовать}} \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{\ru{на}-} and \emph{\ru{след}} \textquotedblleft{}a track\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): what comes after, in the footsteps of the dead.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
